Aerial Wildlife Survey Report 
Hay-Zama Wood Bison Aerial Survey (2024) 
Background 
The Hay-Zama wood bison population (Bison bison 
athabascae) was established through the introduction 
of wood bison to the area. This was part of a national 
effort to recover wood bison populations and the 
establish free ranging, self-sustaining and disease-free 
wood bison in each of the provinces and territories in 
Western Canada. The Hay-Zama population has 
historically been managed by a regulated hunting season 
to maintain a population objective between 400 and 600 
animals. This objective accomplishes a sustainable 
population while also limiting distribution toward diseased 
bison to the east, in and adjacent to Wood Buffalo 
National Park and helping reduce conflicts in 
communities and roadways. A minimum total count is 
conducted annually in late February or March. All 
bison found are counted and classified as adult or calf 
to determine the herd composition. 
Survey Method 
The 2024 Hay-Zama bison survey was conducted by 
flying transects orientated east-west and spaced one 
degree of latitude apart (roughly one statue mile) 
within the historical range. The search area was 
expanded slightly to the North to cover areas of known 
bison occupancy. The crew consisted of 3 observers in 
a Bell 206 Jet Ranger equipped with bubble windows 
in the rear. Survey speed was approximately 90 to 110 
km per hour. All groups were photographed to confirm 
total counts and classification of adults and calves. 
The adult classification includes juveniles and both 
sexes due to the difficulty in accurately separating 
between sex and age classes. Calves were classified 
based on relatively small size and shorter nasal 
bridge. 
Results and Discussion 
The Hay-Zama bison survey was undertaken from 
March 5 - 7, 2024. A total of 485 bison (394 adults and 
91 calves) were seen in 35 groups. The calf ratio (19 
per cent) was consistent with the previous 5-year 
average.
